They need to revive Sonic like Nintendo did with Donkey Kong Country. A beautiful 2.5d Sonic would be amazing, in all honesty, and I say that as someone who usually leans toward Nintendo and PC. I played the Lost World demo, I wasn't overly impressed. I think all they need is a solid 2.5d game with really good music. Nothing new, fancy, trying to push boundaries, just drop the story and all the stuff Sonic series has accumulated over the years and make a game that's fun to play and has amazing music, like the Genesis games had.

Realistically, I don't understand why Sonic doesn't get the same treatment Mario gets. Mario gets (or got, depend on Super Mario Maker's influence) a 2d version and a 3d version of the game. I hate to say it, but Sonic and Mario have always been perfect examples of a series that butchered itself and one that does the vast majority of things right. Sonic needs to start emulating how Mario is handle. Sonic games don't need to become Mario clones, but they need to follow the same principles Mario focuses on: going back to the roots, allowing for cruft to be cut out, not being afraid to revive old ideas, massively improving new ideas, etc.

Look at the level development of Mario as a whole. It's followed a simple formula of trying to make the best level designs possible. You can see how Nintendo started playing with the ideas of all of this in SMB and SMB2 (Lost Levels). SMB2LL was basically them trolling you doing dick things with level design, and SMB1 was Nintendo trying to make the game easy to understand without explicitly telling you that. And in the end with got 3D World, where the level design revolves around introducing a unique mechanic in each level and developing it with the player, in a way teaching them.

And it's seemed to me (I'm not Sonic expert or massive fan but I have enjoyed a few games) that Sonic has just been throwing things at the wall and seeing what sticks. They don't need to step away from Sonic. They need a plan, to say something like, "in 5 years, we want to have a good Sonic game that's 2.5d". Release one game, understanding it'll be mediocre, get feedback, develop it, and then take what you learned and just make a sequel that's just an improvement over the older game.

I think all they need is a solid 2.5d game with really good music.

We got a taste of that with Sonic Generations, but that was an oddity more than a trend. I agree completely that they need to adjust how they release Sonic games, and your Sonic and Mario analysis is spot on.

Funny you should mention Donkey Kong Country. I think it was successful for a few reasons, but none of them really had anything to do with the Donkey Kong, really.

First, let's be fair, DKC didn't look like anything else on the market at the time and that look did a lot to get people to pay attention to it and give it a try. It's distinctive look did a lot to help keep it from mingling with the competition. In 1994 in the platforming genre there was good competition like Earthworm Jim, Aladdin, Mega Man X2... plus the usual suite of forgettable cartoon tie-ins. Gex might have been the closest out there to threaten the style but it didn't really treat the backgrounds as nicely as the sprites, where as DKC gave everything a graphical loving touch.

And it coincided with a turnaround in Nintendo advertising with the whole Play It Loud movement, a newly re-energized marketing campaign that sought to shed the image that Nintendo was just for kids, particularly considering the testimony they gave before congress on the whole video game violence thing and the reality that the Genesis version of Mortal Kombat was pretty much the definitive one because they lacked the censorship.

Modern Sonic games, well, look like just about anything else aimed at kids. They didn't really have a look of their own with the exception of the signature checkerboard pattern on natural green fields and hills, and rings. Sonic Boom was a move to actually look really nice and distinctive but, alas, they forgot that they need a good, playable game too, not just a good engine. Which brings me to:

Second point, it's a good game on it's own. If you remove all the references to previously established Nintendo characters, what do you have? The enemies, the animal friends, the levels, the bosses.... everything is original. It could have been Squishy Bag Country and collected bean bag chair beads instead of bananas and it still would have done well. Modern Sonic games aren't about being a good game, they're about making a Sonic game. They fall over themselves to cram in the Sonic universe and crowd of furry friends and pay no attention to whether things should be tossed together.

They keep rebooting Sonic and I think you're right in that they're just trying to see what sticks. But they want to have their cake and eat it too: Sonic can get rebooted but all the established cast of characters come along for the ride too. Eggman can't be the bad guy because he's just too silly, so now throw in a bunch of "true" villains on top of it. Yuck.

Really, they just need to let someone take the reigns and then trust the creative process to make something worthwhile, not a bunch of edicts to keep the same old chains attached.
